cards.summary: Pattern brush from the Borders_Decorative border library. Large two-tone scallop tiles, half black and half tan-gold, that read like a twisted shaded ribbon. On the 300 pt test curve only a few tiles fit, and they turned the smooth S into big arcs with sharp cusps. (Thumbnail: the brush applied by script to a 300 pt S-curve with a 1 pt stroke in its library document.)
use_for: scalloped frames around large labels, badges or panels
avoid: short or tightly curved paths: the large tiles distort the path shape (seen in the render); lower the stroke weight or use a longer path

recolouring to a brand palette: the colours are part of the tiles; whether the stroke colour tints them depends on the brush's Colorization setting (Brush Options), which was not checked; otherwise Object > Expand Appearance and recolour
cards.applies_to: a stroked path item (open or closed; made for rules and frames); a Pattern brush (Adobe PatternOnPath Brush Tool / Pattern Brush Plugin) that repeats its tile along the path, its size following the stroke weight. Corner tiles were not seen (the test path has no corners). The brush must exist in the target document.
cards.how_to_apply: Panel: Window > Brush Libraries > Borders > Borders_Decorative, select a path, click 'Scallops'. Script: app.open("C:/Program Files/Adobe/Adobe Illustrator 2026/Presets/en_US/Brushes/Borders/Borders_Decorative.ai"), doc.brushes.getByName("Scallops").applyTo(pathItem) on a path in that document, item.duplicate(target.layers[0], ElementPlacement.PLACEATEND) (the brush arrives in the target document), then close the library with SaveOptions.DONOTSAVECHANGES.

verified.note: A few large black and tan-gold scallop tiles that bend the S into arcs with sharp cusps.

cards.name: Sonata
cards.summary: Pattern brush from the Borders_Decorative border library. A bold black band: a heavy rule with a thinner parallel line, topped on one side by a row of curled scroll motifs like lace scallops: strong and graphic. (Thumbnail: the brush applied by script to a 300 pt S-curve with a 1 pt stroke in its library document.)
avoid: the motif on the wrong side of a frame: it sits on one side of the path only; flip it with Object > Path > Reverse Path Direction
small output: the curls clog
